o: Each word can be rearranged independently, so the answer is the product over words of (length)! / (count of each letter)!. For "too hot": 3!/2! × 3! = 3 × 6 = 18. With word lengths up to 10⁵, compute factorials mod 10⁹+7 and divide using modular inverses via Fermat's little theorem (mod is prime, so x⁻¹ = x^(mod−2)).
k: Words are independent — multiply per-word multinomial coefficients.
Modular division via Fermat: inv(x) = x^(MOD−2) since MOD = 10⁹+7 is prime.
Precompute factorials once up to the max word length.

a.i: For each word, compute len! × Π inv(cnt_c!) using precomputed factorials and fast exponentiation; multiply everything mod 10⁹+7.
s: Split s on spaces; for each word, tally letter counts.
Multiply answer by fact[len] × Π pow(fact[cnt], p−2, p) mod p.
a.t: O(L + W·26·log MOD) — factorial precomputation is O(L); per word we do ≤26 modular exponentiations.

w: Single standard approach. Pitfalls: dividing naively instead of using modular inverse, recomputing factorials per word, and forgetting words of length 1 contribute factor 1. Follow-up: count anagrams avoiding a forbidden word, or compute the k-th lexicographic anagram.
